title: Kramastotra — Hymn of the Successive
author: Ascribed to Abhinavagupta
text:
The Kramastotra is a hymn of thirty verses on the krama — the succession or wave-process that is the heart of the Trika's fierce goddess worship, transmitted in the GRETIL recension under Abhinavagupta's name. Krama names the ordered unfolding of the divine powers, successive moment to moment, and the hymn both describes that rite of completion amid sorrow and performs its mood: mirrored mind drops its fear, the self is redoubled, and the addresses of the thirty verses move through invocation, consecration and praise.

Its juice: the successive is not a ladder climbed once but the Real's own pulse. To stand inside krama — thought following thought as wave follows wave without a fixed observer behind them — is the rite that ends sorrow; the hymn's thirty stanzas are steps that dissolve as they are taken.
